cs.t: Earlier this week I purchased a Casio Waveceptor watch. It features the ability to synchronize with this radio signal. I'm very happy with it. I was also happy with an early-2000s model for several years prior. The older one's receiver seemed to become unreliable after about a decade, possibly due to changes in the wireless spectrum over time. Overall, it was quite a reliable watch and so I have good confidence in this product line.

In Japan they sell the Waveceptor brand Casio watches. I got a nice simple titanium (case back and strap) with solar, LCD alarms and radio control for around $200. It even auto re-centers the hands if they are exposed to strong magnets.
You can also get these on eBay and Amazon though 3rd sellers.
cs.th: Canada's only watchmaking school still ticking after 80 years

cs.t: I live just beyond the fringe zone for reception of WWVB on my Casio Waveceptor. Depending on solar conditions, and how I leave the watch overnight (south-east facing window with space to a metal window frame for a coupling effect), I can get it to sync once in a while.
If you're interested in buying a Casio watch that does this they tend to be called Waveceptor, I'd recommend looking at one that's also solar powered (tough solar).
